newsitem.title: UK: Harding estate to sell Chelsea soccer stake - report.
newsitem.headline: Harding estate to sell Chelsea soccer stake - report.

text.p: The estate of Matthew Harding, who died in a helicopter crash in October 1996, intends to sell his stake in Chelsea Village Plc, the holding company that owns Chelsea football club, the Sunday Times newspaper reported.
The estate increased its holding in the club to 27.34 percent in January by exercising an option for 7.5 million new shares.
Chelsea clinched the English FA Cup on Saturday with a 2-0 win over Middlesbrough, the London club's first Cup win since 1970.
The Sunday Times quoted sources close to Harding's estate as saying they intend to liquidate the holding, valued at around 50 million pounds ($81.8 million) and to retain only a small stake.
Chelsea's controversial chairman Ken Bates, who had a volatile relationship with Harding, has warned potential buyers that they would not be offered a seat on the board. ($ = 0.611 British Pounds)
